## Find the radius of c
Circle $c$ touches all four sides, so its diameter equals the side of the square, 12 cm.
r &= \frac{12}{2}
&= 6
## Find the area of c
\text{Area} &= \pi r^2
&= \pi (6)^2
&= 36\pi
&= 113.097\ldots
&\approx 113.10
ANSWER: r = 6 \text{ cm};\ \text{Area} = 113.10 \text{ cm}^2

## Find the area of the square
\text{Square} &= 12 \times 12
&= 144
## Divide the circle area by the square area
\text{Percentage} &= \frac{113.10}{144} \times 100
&= 0.7854 \times 100
&= 78.54
&\approx 79\%
ANSWER: 79\%

## Use the right-angled triangle from the centre
The radius of $k$ is the distance from the centre to a corner. It is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with both legs equal to 6 cm (half a side).
## Apply Pythagoras
r^2 &= 6^2 + 6^2
&= 36 + 36
&= 72
## Take the square root and round
r &= \sqrt{72}
&= 8.4853\ldots
&\approx 8.49 \text{ cm}
ANSWER: r = 8.49 \text{ cm}

## Mark B on the given line
Use a ruler to measure 8 cm from $A$ along the line and mark the point $B$.
## Draw the 130° angle at B
Place the protractor at $B$ with its base along $BA$.
Mark 130° from $BA$, on the upper side of the line, and join it to $B$.
This ray makes 50° with the line extended beyond $B$.
## Mark C on the ray
Measure 6 cm from $B$ along the ray and mark $C$.
## Find D with two arcs
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal: $|AD| = |BC| = 6$ cm and $|DC| = |AB| = 8$ cm.
With the compass on $A$, draw an arc of radius 6 cm above the line.
With the compass on $C$, draw an arc of radius 8 cm. It meets the first arc at $D$.
## Complete the parallelogram
Join $A$ to $D$ and $D$ to $C$ to finish $ABCD$.
ANSWER: ABCD \text{ with } |AB| = 8,\ |BC| = 6,\ |\angle ABC| = 130^\circ

## Opposite angles are equal: find x
$(2x-30)^\circ$ is opposite the $100^\circ$ angle, so they are equal.
2x - 30 &= 100
2x &= 130
x &= 65
## Adjacent angles sum to 180°
$(x+3y)^\circ$ and $100^\circ$ are adjacent angles, so they add to $180^\circ$.
x + 3y + 100 &= 180
x + 3y &= 80
## Substitute x = 65 and solve for y
65 + 3y &= 80
3y &= 80 - 65
3y &= 15
y &= 5
ANSWER: x = 65,\ y = 5

## Recall what makes a parallelogram
A parallelogram is a four-sided shape whose opposite sides are parallel and equal in length.
## Check a square against this
A square has opposite sides parallel and equal in length.
So every square is a parallelogram: the statement is True.
ANSWER: \text{True}

## Substitute into the gradient formula
Gradient as a percentage is $\dfrac{|BC|}{|AC|} \times 100$.
\text{Gradient} &= \frac{24}{135} \times 100
## Evaluate and round to the nearest percent
&= 17.78\%
&\approx 18\%
ANSWER: 18\%

## Write Pythagoras for the right-angled triangle
$[AB]$ is the hypotenuse, so $|AC|^2 + |BC|^2 = |AB|^2$. Let $x = |AC|$.
x^2 + 27^2 &= 105^2
## Square the numbers
x^2 + 729 &= 11025
## Subtract 729 from both sides
x^2 &= 11025 - 729
x^2 &= 10296
## Take the positive square root
A length is positive, so use the positive root only.
x &= \sqrt{10296}
x &= 101.469
|AC| &\approx 101 \text{ m}
ANSWER: |AC| = 101 \text{ m}

## Write the gradient as a tangent
Gradient is $\dfrac{|BC|}{|AC|} = \tan A$, and 9% means $\dfrac{9}{100}$.
\tan A &= \frac{9}{100}
## Use the inverse tangent
Make sure the calculator is in degree mode.
A &= \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{9}{100}\right)
A &= 5.1427^\circ
A &\approx 5^\circ
ANSWER: \angle BAC = 5^\circ

## Find the radius
The radius is half the diameter.
r &= \frac{2.4}{2}
&= 1.2 \text{ m}
## Substitute into the volume of a cylinder
The water depth is $h = 0.75$ m, so $V = \pi r^2 h$.
V &= \pi (1.2)^2 (0.75)
## Evaluate and round to 2 decimal places
&= 3.3929
&\approx 3.39 \text{ m}^3
ANSWER: V = 3.39 \text{ m}^3

## Find the volume of one cube
A cube with side 0.5 m has volume length $\times$ width $\times$ height.
V &= 0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.5
&= 0.125 \text{ m}^3
## Multiply by 3 seats
\text{Total} &= 3 \times 0.125
&= 0.375 \text{ m}^3
ANSWER: \text{Total volume} = 0.375 \text{ m}^3

## Substitute into the curved surface area formula
Curved surface area of a cone is $\pi r l$, with $r = 1.3$ and $l = 1.53$.
\text{C.S.A.} &= \pi (1.3)(1.53)
## Evaluate and round to 2 decimal places
&= 6.2486
&\approx 6.25 \text{ m}^2
ANSWER: 6.25 \text{ m}^2

## Write down x
The sector's radius is the slant height of the cone.
x &= 1.53 \text{ m}
## Equate the sector area to the curved surface area
The net folds into the cone, so the sector's area equals the C.S.A. $6.25$ m$^2$.
\frac{A}{360} \times \pi r^2 &= 6.25
## Make A the subject
A &= \frac{6.25 \times 360}{\pi (1.53)^2}
## Evaluate and round to the nearest degree
A &= 305.95
A &\approx 306^\circ
ANSWER: x = 1.53 \text{ m},\ A = 306^\circ

## (i) Pick the classes that could be over 100
The class 90 to 120 includes students above 100, and every class above it is entirely above 100.
At most, all 59 students in 90 to 120 read for more than 100 minutes.
## (i) Add the frequencies
\text{Maximum} &= 59 + 18 + 10
&= 87
## (iii) Say why the sampling method is limited
Only the first 200 students to arrive were asked, so the sample is not random.
These could be local students, or students arriving together on school buses.
Students who arrive later are left out, so the sample may not be representative.
ANSWER: 87 \text{ students}

## Locate the median position
There are 200 students, so the median lies between the 100th and 101st values.
## Add up the frequencies from the first class
16 + 35 &= 51
16 + 35 + 62 &= 113
After 30 to 60 only 51 students are counted, and after 60 to 90 it is 113.
## Identify the median class
The 100th and 101st students are both in the 60 to 90 class, so the median is somewhere in that class. The exact value cannot be found from grouped data.
ANSWER: 60 \le \text{median} < 90

## Choose a histogram
The data is grouped into classes of equal width (30 minutes), so a histogram works, with bar heights equal to the frequencies.
## Set up and label the axes
Put minutes read per day on the horizontal axis, marked 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180.
Put number of students on the vertical axis, from 0 to 70.
## Draw one bar for each class
The bar heights are 16, 35, 62, 59, 18 and 10, with no gaps between bars.
ANSWER: \text{Histogram with bar heights } 16, 35, 62, 59, 18, 10

## Write the sample proportion
$\hat{p}$ is the number rated Excellent divided by the sample size.
\hat{p} &= \frac{61}{500}
&= 0.122
## Convert to a percentage
0.122 \times 100 &= 12.2\%
ANSWER: 12.2\%

## Substitute n = 500 into the margin of error
The margin of error is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, with $n = 500$.
\text{Margin of error} &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{500}}
&= 0.044721
## Convert to a percentage and round
0.044721 \times 100 &= 4.4721\%
4.4721\% &\approx 4.5\%
ANSWER: \text{Margin of error} = 4.5\%

## Form the interval around the sample proportion
The interval is $\hat{p} \pm$ margin of error, using $\hat{p} = 12.2\%$ and margin $4.5\%$.
12.2 - 4.5 \le p &\le 12.2 + 4.5
7.7 \le p &\le 16.7
## Compare with the population percentage
The population percentage, 10%, lies inside the interval from 7.7% to 16.7%.
## State the conclusion and reason
Conclusion: there is no difference between the Cork percentage and the population percentage, so the claim is not supported at the 5% level.
Reason: 10% is inside the interval, within the confidence interval.
ANSWER: 7.7\% \le p \le 16.7\%,\ \text{10\% is inside, so no difference}

## Find the base angle of triangle OBC
$|OB| = |OC|$, so triangle $OBC$ is isosceles and its base angles are equal.
Angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$, and $|\angle BOC| = 72^\circ$.
|\angle OBC| &= \frac{180 - 72}{2}
&= 54^\circ
## Double it to get the angle of the pentagon
$OB$ splits angle $CBA$ into two equal angles, each $54^\circ$.
|\angle CBA| &= 2 \times 54
&= 108^\circ
ANSWER: |\angle CBA| = 108^\circ

## Area of triangle AOB using two sides and the angle
Two sides are $|AO| = |BO| = 6$ and the angle between them is $72^\circ$, so use $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
\text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2}(6)(6)\sin 72^\circ
&= 17.119
&\approx 17.1 \text{ cm}^2
## Multiply by 5 for the pentagon
The pentagon is made of five congruent triangles.
\text{Area of pentagon} &= 5 \times 17.119
&= 85.595
&\approx 85.6 \text{ cm}^2
ANSWER: \text{Triangle} = 17.1 \text{ cm}^2,\ \text{Pentagon} = 85.6 \text{ cm}^2

## Set up the pairs
Write each outcome as (first spin, second spin). Each spin has 5 possible results, so there are $5 \times 5 = 25$ outcomes.
## List the outcomes by first spin
First spin 1: $(1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (1,4), (1,5)$
First spin 2: $(2,1), (2,2), (2,3), (2,4), (2,5)$
First spin 3: $(3,1), (3,2), (3,3), (3,4), (3,5)$
First spin 4: $(4,1), (4,2), (4,3), (4,4), (4,5)$
First spin 5: $(5,1), (5,2), (5,3), (5,4), (5,5)$
ANSWER: \text{25 outcomes, from } (1,1) \text{ to } (5,5)

## Maximum: add the two largest numbers
\text{Maximum} &= 5 + 5
&= 10
## Minimum: add the two smallest numbers
\text{Minimum} &= 1 + 1
&= 2
ANSWER: \text{Maximum} = 10,\ \text{Minimum} = 2

## Write the expected value formula
Expected value is the sum of each amount multiplied by its probability.
E(x) &= \sum x \, P(x)
## Substitute the amounts and probabilities
E(x) &= 1(0.3) + 0.5(0.2) + 0(0.4) + 5(0.1)
## Multiply each term, then add
&= 0.3 + 0.1 + 0 + 0.5
&= 0.90
## Compare with the cost to play
Jena pays 1 euro to play, but her expected winnings are only 0.90 euro.
The expected value is not equal to the cost, so the game is not fair.
ANSWER: E(x) = \text{€}0.90 < \text{€}1\text{, so the game is not fair}

## Square both sides
n - 3 &= \sqrt{3n+1}
(n-3)^2 &= 3n + 1
## Expand the bracket
n^2 - 6n + 9 &= 3n + 1
## Collect everything on one side
n^2 - 6n + 9 - 3n - 1 &= 0
n^2 - 9n + 8 &= 0
## Factorise and solve
(n-8)(n-1) &= 0
n &= 8 \text{ or } n = 1
## Check both answers in the original equation
Squaring can introduce a false solution, so test each value in $n-3=\sqrt{3n+1}$.
n = 1:\quad 1 - 3 &= -2 \text{ but } \sqrt{3(1)+1} = 2
The two sides differ, so $n = 1$ is rejected.
n = 8:\quad 8 - 3 &= 5 \text{ and } \sqrt{3(8)+1} = \sqrt{25} = 5
The two sides agree, so $n = 8$ is the solution.
ANSWER: n = 8

## Label the equations
x + 2y &= 143 \quad (1)
y + 3w &= -74 \quad (2)
4x + 5w &= 4 \quad (3)
## Eliminate y from (1) and (2)
Multiply (2) by $-2$ so the $y$ terms cancel when added to (1).
-2y - 6w &= 148 \quad (2\text{ times }-2)
Add this to (1).
x - 6w &= 291 \quad (4)
## Eliminate x from (3) and (4)
Multiply (4) by 4 so the $x$ terms match (3).
4x - 24w &= 1164 \quad (5)
Subtract (3) from (5).
4x - 24w - (4x + 5w) &= 1164 - 4
4x - 24w - 4x - 5w &= 1164 - 4
-29w &= 1160
## Solve for w
w &= \frac{1160}{-29}
w &= -40
## Substitute w = -40 into (4) to find x
x - 6(-40) &= 291
x + 240 &= 291
x &= 51
## Substitute x = 51 into (1) to find y
51 + 2y &= 143
2y &= 92
y &= 46
ANSWER: x = 51,\ y = 46,\ w = -40

## Identify a, b and c
z^2 + 12z + 261 &= 0
Here $a = 1$, $b = 12$, $c = 261$.
## Substitute into the quadratic formula
z &= \frac{-12 \pm \sqrt{12^2 - 4(1)(261)}}{2(1)}
## Simplify under the square root
z &= \frac{-12 \pm \sqrt{144 - 1044}}{2}
z &= \frac{-12 \pm \sqrt{-900}}{2}
## Write the root using i
$\sqrt{-900} = \sqrt{900} \times \sqrt{-1} = 30i$.
z &= \frac{-12 \pm 30i}{2}
## Divide each term by 2
z &= -6 \pm 15i
z &= -6 + 15i \text{ or } z = -6 - 15i
ANSWER: -6 + 15i \text{ and } -6 - 15i

## Find the modulus r
For $1 - \sqrt{3}i$ the real part is $1$ and the imaginary part is $-\sqrt{3}$.
r &= \sqrt{1^2 + (-\sqrt{3})^2}
&= \sqrt{1 + 3}
&= \sqrt{4}
&= 2
## Find the argument
The point $(1, -\sqrt{3})$ lies in the fourth quadrant.
\tan\alpha &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{1}
\alpha &= \frac{\pi}{3}
In the fourth quadrant the argument is negative.
\theta &= -\frac{\pi}{3}
## Write in polar form
1 - \sqrt{3}i &= 2\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)
## Apply de Moivre's theorem
$\left[r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\right]^n = r^n(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)$.
(1 - \sqrt{3}i)^9 &= 2^9\left(\cos\left(9 \times -\frac{\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(9 \times -\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)
&= 512\left(\cos(-3\pi) + i\sin(-3\pi)\right)
## Evaluate and write as a + bi
$\cos(-3\pi) = -1$ and $\sin(-3\pi) = 0$.
&= 512(-1 + 0i)
&= -512
ANSWER: -512

## Use the rule for integrating cos(ax)
$\int \cos ax \, dx = \frac{1}{a}\sin ax + C$. Here $a = 6$.
## Write the integral
\int \cos 6x \, dx &= \frac{1}{6}\sin 6x + C
ANSWER: \frac{1}{6}\sin 6x + C

## Find the point of contact
f(2) &= 2(2)^3 - 9(2)^2 + 5(2) - 11
&= 16 - 36 + 10 - 11
&= -21
The point is $(2, -21)$.
## Differentiate f(x)
f'(x) &= 6x^2 - 18x + 5
## Find the slope at x = 2
f'(2) &= 6(2)^2 - 18(2) + 5
&= 24 - 36 + 5
&= -7
## Write the equation of the tangent
Use $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$ with $m = -7$ and $(x_1, y_1) = (2, -21)$.
y - (-21) &= -7(x - 2)
ANSWER: y - (-21) = -7(x - 2)

## Differentiate twice
f'(x) &= 6x^2 - 18x + 5
f''(x) &= 12x - 18
## Set the second derivative to zero
A point of inflection is where $f''(x) = 0$.
12x - 18 &= 0
## Solve for x
12x &= 18
x &= \frac{18}{12}
x &= \frac{3}{2}
ANSWER: x = \frac{3}{2}

## Find the slope of l
$l$ passes through $(6, 0)$ and $(10, 2)$.
m &= \frac{2 - 0}{10 - 6}
&= \frac{1}{2}
## Translate the condition into a slope
$l'(x) = \frac{1}{2}$ for every $x$, since $l$ is a straight line.
So $p'(x) = l'(x)$ means the tangent to $p$ has slope $\frac{1}{2}$, parallel to $l$.
## Draw the two parallel tangents
Place a ruler along $l$ and slide it down and to the left until it just touches the curve near the lower left. Draw this tangent in blue.
Slide it up and to the right until it just touches the curve near the maximum. Draw this second tangent in blue.
## Read the x-values from the touching points
Draw a vertical line from each touching point down to the x-axis and read off the values.
The first touches at about $x = 2.2$ and the second at about $x = 6.8$.
ANSWER: x \approx 2.2 \text{ and } x \approx 6.8

## Find f(x + h)
First principles uses $f'(x)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$.
f(x+h) &= (x+h)^2 - 7(x+h) - 10
&= x^2 + 2hx + h^2 - 7x - 7h - 10
## Find f(x + h) − f(x)
f(x+h) - f(x) &= x^2 + 2hx + h^2 - 7x - 7h - 10 - (x^2 - 7x - 10)
&= x^2 + 2hx + h^2 - 7x - 7h - 10 - x^2 + 7x + 10
&= 2hx + h^2 - 7h
## Divide by h
\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} &= \frac{2hx + h^2 - 7h}{h}
&= \frac{2hx}{h} + \frac{h^2}{h} - \frac{7h}{h}
&= 2x + h - 7
## Let h tend to 0
f'(x) &= \lim_{h \to 0} (2x + h - 7)
&= 2x + 0 - 7
&= 2x - 7
ANSWER: f'(x) = 2x - 7

## State the answer
The statement is false.
## Justify using the meaning of local minimum
A local minimum at $(0,5)$ only means $h(x)\ge 5$ for $x$ close to $0$.
Away from $x=0$ the graph can turn and fall below $5$, for example a cubic with a local minimum at $(0,5)$ that goes to $-\infty$.
So $h(x)$ need not be at least $5$ for all real $x$.
ANSWER: \text{False}
